readingInstruction: Read Hosea 4:1-7:16. The prophet now brings God’s charges against Israel: no knowledge of God, empty worship, and a heart that is like a morning cloud. These chapters include the unit’s anchor verse, Hosea 6:6. Read it in its setting.
settingTheScene: The second part of Hosea consists of a series of oracles that mix accusation and pleading. God has a lawsuit against Israel. The charge is unfaithfulness to the covenant: idolatry, injustice, and a lack of the knowledge of God. The priests and the political leaders are especially blamed. The section includes a beautiful invitation to return and a sharp reply that shows how shallow Israel’s repentance was.
observation: “Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a controversy with the inhabitants of the land. There is no faithfulness or steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land” (4:1).
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me” (4:6).
“A spirit of whoredom has led them astray, and they have left their God to play the whore” (4:12).
“Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone” (4:17).
“Come, let us return to the LORD; for he has torn us, that he may heal us; he has struck us down, and he will bind us up” (6:1).
“Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD; his going out is sure as the dawn” (6:3).
“What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away” (6:4).
“For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings” (6:6).
interpretation:
The lawsuit begins with a three-part diagnosis: no faithfulness, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God. The first two are relational. The third is the root. The people had stopped knowing God. They no longer understood who he was or what he wanted. As a result, the society fell apart: swearing, lying, murder, stealing, adultery. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” The knowledge in view is not just information but a relationship, the knowledge of a husband and wife. It is the loss of intimacy with God.

Priests are especially blamed. They fed on the sin of the people, wanting them to sin so that the offerings would increase. A priesthood that profits from the sins of the people has lost its purpose.

Chapter 6 opens with what sounds like a model of repentance: “Come, let us return to the LORD.” The words are beautiful. They acknowledge that God has torn and will heal, that he will revive them after two days. But God’s response is devastating: “What shall I do with you?” He knows how shallow it is. “Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away.” Their repentance burns off with the morning sun. It is a feeling, not a commitment.

Then comes the unit’s anchor verse. “For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.” The people thought that offering sacrifices would fix the relationship. God says that what he wants is a heart that loves and knows him. It does not make sacrifice meaningless, since God himself commanded it. It means that sacrifice without love is empty.

Chapter 7 continues with a series of pictures of Israel’s folly: a cake that is burned on one side and raw on the other, a silly dove flitting between Egypt and Assyria. Israel is half-baked, unstable, and turning to the wrong help. “They do not cry to me from the heart.”
connection: Jesus quotes Hosea 6:6 twice: when defending his eating with sinners (Matthew 9:13) and when defending his disciples on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:7). He told the Pharisees, “Go and learn what this means.” John 17:3 says, “This is eternal life, that they know you the only true God.” Paul longs to know Christ (Philippians 3:10). Hebrews 13:15-16 says that the sacrifices pleasing to God are praise and doing good.
application:
Take Hosea 6:6 with you, and let it search you.

Ask whether your repentance has been like a morning cloud. What would a lasting change look like?

Make time to know God, not just to do things for him.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you desire to know him, and ask him to keep your love from fading like a morning cloud.
Confess where religious activity has replaced your heart.
Ask him to teach you to love steadfastly.
